question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼B(150,0.48),$ use the normal approximation to the binomial distribution to approximate $P(X=67).$ Give your final answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.9\,$ | $\,0.1841\,$ | $\,0.1814\,$ | $\,0.1788\,$ | $\,0.1762\,$ | $\,0.1736\,$ |
| $\,-0.8\,$ | $\,0.2119\,$ | $\,0.2090\,$ | $\,0.2061\,$ | $\,0.2033\,$ | $\,0.2005\,$ |
| $\,-0.7\,$ | $\,0.2420\,$ | $\,0.2389\,$ | $\,0.2358\,$ | $\,0.2327\,$ | $\,0.2297\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=150$ and $p=0.48.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =150\cdot 0.48 \\  & =72 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =150\cdot (1-0.48) \\  & =78 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(150)(0.48)=72
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(150)(0.48)(1-0.48)=37.44.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(72,37.44).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=67).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=67)≈P(66.5\le Y\le 67.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(66.5\le Y\le 67.5) & =P(\frac{66.5-72}{\sqrt{37.44}}\le Z\le \frac{67.5-72}{\sqrt{37.44}}) \\  & ≈P(-0.90\le Z\le -0.74) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.74)-P(Z<-0.90) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.74)-P(Z\le -0.90) \\  & =Φ(-0.74)-Φ(-0.90) \\  & =0.2297-0.1841 \\  & =0.046\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=67)≈0.046.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0468.$
